Economist/YouGov and Emerson each had the Democratic lead on generic ballots sitting at around 8 percentage points, but for Emerson's poll, that was down from an 11.4 percentage point lead the previous month. [...] Another finding across multiple polls was a slight edge by Democrats on the generic ballot in the upcoming midterm elections.

In Marquette's August poll, 46% of registered voters preferred Democrats on the generic ballot, compared with 44% for Republicans. Among likely voters, though, the Democrats' lead over Republicans increased, with 51% of likely voters saying they would vote for the Democratic candidate in their districts, and only 45% preferring the Republican candidate. results.content: In the 2026 state House elections, Democrats hope to break the Republicans’ supermajority. The August SLU/YouGov Poll asked likely voters, using a generic-ballot format, how they would vote in their local state House district; 48% said Republican and 44% said Democratic, with 8% not sure. Independents favored Democratic candidates, 42% to 36%.
